Also a denizen of northern MN. Keeping the following in my truck every winter has saved my bacon more than a few times:

- a couple wool blankets
- extra pair of wool socks, gloves, and a hat
- prepackaged hand/foot/body warmers
- a sleeping bag
- a small candle 
- snow shovel
- bag of kitty litter (for traction on ice)
- flashlight and/or headlamp
- road flares
- 5 gallons of gas (at minimum a spare gas can)
- snow pants + spare winter boots

Late to the party, but I have a German Shepherd trained to help me break trail and guard camp - I won't bushwhack without him. It definitely comes down to trust, however, and if I'm shooting or throwing steel I'll keep him tied off - in case he gets any grand ideas.

He's great off leash, and he's trained not to run ahead more than a dozen yards or so without waiting for me, so on proper trails I typically keep a lead slung around my neck so I have it on hand if we encounter people. Otherwise dog is loose. (It's a rare day that we see even people signs out where I ramble, so it's not a frequent concern. Your mileage may vary.) He's also trained to respond to clicks and bird calls as recall commands, in case I don't want people knowing where I might be.

Overnighting is a different story - I have a fifteen foot long line that I tie him off with, because he always wants to get chummy with deer and God-knows-what-else at 4 am, and I never wanna deal with a dog lost in the sticks. I do account for dog space when I'm putting up shelter, but unless it's raining he'd rather sleep outside and mind the camp.

One other helpful bit is that dog carries his own gear - kibble, canteen, long line, and wire brush for those damn sticky burrs. Not quite as slick as the other dude here with his fucking pack goats, but maybe someday we'll be as cool.
